item.title: Optimized costimulatory domains boost tumor killing in CAR NK cells
item.description: Researchers at the Ribeirão Preto Blood Center and the Center for Cell-Based Therapy (CTC) conducted a study using the NK-92 cell line to test new models of chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) with specific costimulatory domains, such as 2B4 and DAP12.

item.title: Tropical cyclones linked to rise in drug-related deaths months after landfall
item.description: Tropical cyclones, including hurricanes and tropical storms, are linked to increased rates of drug-related deaths up to three months after the storm passes-particularly in higher-income, White communities and among younger populations.

item.title: Cannabis use in adolescence associated with higher rates of psychiatric disorders
item.description: Adolescents who use cannabis could face a significantly higher risk of developing serious psychiatric disorders by young adulthood, according to a large new study published today in JAMA Health Forum.

item.title: Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities face severe mental health disparities
item.description: Adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities, such as autism and Down syndrome, experience substantially higher rates of anxiety and depression than the general population of adults, researchers reported today in JAMA Network Open.

item.title: Discovery offers hope for reducing immune-related heart risks in cancer patients
item.description: For many people diagnosed with cancer, treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has dramatically extended lives.

item.title: Milken Institute and Ann Theodore Foundation fund mTOR inhibitor trial for sarcoidosis
item.description: The Milken Institute Science Philanthropy Accelerator for Research and Collaboration (SPARC), in partnership with the Ann Theodore Foundation (ATF), has launched a new funding program to support a future clinical trial in cutaneous sarcoidosis.

item.title: Social media exposure associated with steroid use intentions among boys and men
item.description: A new study of more than 1,500 boys and men in Canada and the United States suggests that social media may play a meaningful role in shaping intentions to use anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS), particularly when users are exposed to muscularity-focused content and engage in body comparisons online.

item.title: Smarter timing of cancer treatments could improve cure rates, study suggests
item.description: A new study provides hope that smarter timing of cancer treatments could improve cure rates.

item.title: Single prenatal exposure to fungicide linked to disease across 20 generations
item.description: A single exposure to a toxic fungicide during pregnancy can increase the risk of disease for 20 subsequent generations - with inherited health problems worsening many generations after exposure.

item.title: Indoor air quality plays major role in adult asthma symptoms
item.description: For adults with asthma, having fans, air purifiers or other ventilation and exhaust systems - especially in kitchens and bathrooms - is one of the best ways to reduce the risk of flare-ups at home.
